name: Firecrawl API
description: Firecrawl v2 API — turn any URL or search query into clean, LLM-ready markdown. POST /v2/scrape fetches a single page, POST /v2/search runs a web search and returns full page content, POST /v2/map lists a site's URLs, POST /v2/crawl and POST /v2/batch/scrape start async jobs polled via GET /v2/crawl/{id} and GET /v2/batch/scrape/{id}, and POST /v2/extract pulls structured data from pages using a prompt or JSON schema. Also available: POST /v2/agent (autonomous browsing tasks), POST /v2/parse (parse a document such as a PDF into markdown), and /v2/monitor/* (scheduled recurring crawls). Firecrawl's own per-request `timeout` field maxes out at 300000ms, but drawlatch caps this connection at 120000ms — comfortably above Firecrawl's own 30s scrape and 60s search defaults, and enough for realistic synchronous work. Use the async crawl/batch job pattern for anything longer rather than holding a socket open. Screenshots are returned as public Supabase URLs on a different host, which this connection's allowlist deliberately rejects: fetch them out-of-band rather than through the proxy, so the API key is never sent to them. Auth is handled automatically via the FIRECRAWL_API_KEY environment variable as a Bearer token.
